title: The seminaries
hook: the great seminaries of Najaf and Qom

segments.voice: Yesterday, the marja', and your line: follow the living scholar. What did you ask, and whom did you ask? Day one thousand two hundred.

Morning, in a narrow lane near a golden dome. Two students sit on a mat with one book open between them. One reads a line and explains it. The other objects. The first pushes back, finds the line again, reads it more slowly. Nobody is angry. This is the work. Yesterday's marja' doesn't appear out of nowhere. He is made, over long years, in lanes and rooms like this one. Today, the places that make them.
screen: `TWO STUDENTS, ONE BOOK.` → `READ, OBJECT, PUSH BACK.` → `WHERE A MARJA' IS MADE.`

segments.voice: The word is hawzah, the Shia seminary. In full, al-hawzah al-'ilmiyyah, the seat of learning. Today's two cities are Najaf and Qom. Najaf, in Iraq, is the city of the shrine of Imam 'Ali. Tradition says its hawzah grew around the scholar Shaykh al-Tusi, who settled there after leaving Baghdad. Qom, in Iran, holds the shrine of Fatimah al-Ma'sumah, sister of Imam al-Rida, and its hawzah was revived in modern times. Both are shrine cities. The study happens in the shadow of the domes. How does it run? In stages, not in fixed years. First come the preliminaries: Arabic grammar, logic, rhetoric. Then the surfaces, the sutuh: set textbooks of law and of its method, read line by line with a teacher. Then the highest stage, bahth al-kharij, study outside the text. A senior teacher lectures on a question with no set book, weighing the evidence and earlier opinions aloud, and students are expected to argue back. Between lessons, students review in pairs, like the two on the mat. A student chooses teachers, sits in their circles, moves on when ready. Out of long years of that comes a mujtahid, someone able to derive rulings. And from among the mujtahids, through the regard of other scholars and the trust of believers, a marja'. Scholars move between the two cities. A student may begin in one and finish in the other. Najaf and Qom aren't rivals in this telling. They're two lamps in the same tradition, on either side of a border.
screen: `HAWZAH: THE SEAT OF LEARNING.` · `NAJAF AND QOM, TWO SHRINE CITIES.` · `GRAMMAR, TEXTBOOKS, BEYOND THE TEXT.` · `FROM STUDENT TO MUJTAHID TO MARJA'.`

segments.voice: The practice: look at Najaf on a map. Find Baghdad, then follow south to Najaf. Notice the town beside it: Kufa, Abu Hanifa's city, from earlier this month. Two schools, close neighbors. Then cross the border east into Iran, and find Qom, south of Tehran. Rest your eyes on each city for a few breaths. Then think of one place where you were really taught something, a classroom, a kitchen, a garage, and the person who taught you. If you pray, you can remember your teachers. The bell holds the time.
Hawzah. The Shia seminary, the seat of learning, with its great centers in Najaf and Qom. Today's word.
Your line: najaf and qom. Today, study one thing properly, with a book or a person, and argue with it a little before you agree. Day one thousand two hundred.

howItsDone: Shia students study at the seminaries of Najaf, Qom and elsewhere, moving from Arabic and logic through set textbooks to advanced lectures beyond the textbook, often reviewing in pairs.

original.note: Arabic: a domain, a seat; al-hawzah al-'ilmiyyah, the seat of learning, the Shia seminary.

trapdoor: what you thought: a seminary is a school for priests.
what it means: the hawzah trains jurists in stages, from grammar to lectures beyond the textbook.
what a scholar hears: muqaddimat, sutuh and bahth al-kharij, and the shrine cities of Najaf and Qom.

sources.ref: Shia seminary curriculum (muqaddimat, sutuh, bahth al-kharij); biographies of Shaykh al-Tusi

notes: Shaykh al-Tusi's move from Baghdad to Najaf and the hawzah growing around him is framed as 'tradition says'; confirm. Dates deliberately omitted.
Qom's hawzah 'revived in modern times' (refounded by Shaykh 'Abd al-Karim Ha'iri Yazdi) is left unnamed and undated; confirm wording.
Fatimah al-Ma'sumah as sister of Imam al-Rida (the eighth Imam): confirm.
Stages (muqaddimat, sutuh, bahth al-kharij) and paired review (mubahathah): confirm descriptions.
'A student chooses teachers and moves on when ready' (no fixed years): confirm as a fair description of the traditional system; some modern hawzah programs have structured years and exams.
'Najaf and Qom aren't rivals in this telling': intended to avoid a ranking or political framing; confirm tone.
Practice geography (Kufa beside Najaf; Qom south of Tehran): confirm.

Editor pass: removed the superlatives 'above all' and 'a great center of study'; corrected 'a short walk apart' (Najaf and Kufa) and 'a border apart' (Najaf and Qom are far apart) to looser, accurate wording.
